show.name: Fi Europe 2026 (Food ingredients Europe)
show.venue: Messe Frankfurt, Ludwig-Erhard-Anlage 1, 60327 Frankfurt am Main
show.notes: Silitex Italy exhibits at Hall 4.1, stand N56 (41N56) — invite visitors back to the stand. Halls read from the stand codes (31D36 = hall 3.1, stand D36); 'SU' stands = start-up area in hall 5.1. Directory snapshot 28/10/2026 (1,532 exhibitors) — re-check stands in the show app. Kosher is claimed only for CPL 350, CPL 350 ET and SILIFOOD 30.

top.what_they_make: Subsidiary of Sudeep Pharma (established 2021) producing food and nutraceutical ingredients, building on the parent's pharma excipient business.
top.why_silitex: Mineral and excipient processing (wet precipitation, spray drying) foams; a powder antifoam (POLIFOOD 1500 S) suits dry blends.
opening_questions: Do any of your precipitation or drying steps foam?
Would a powdered food-contact antifoam be useful in your blends?
Where are your plants and who buys processing aids?
top.avoid: Production is mainly in India; confirm EU or Netherlands operations.

top.what_they_make: Specialty enzyme and biosolutions company combining enzyme expertise, microbiology, bioprocess development and industrial manufacturing.
top.why_silitex: Bioprocess development and industrial enzyme manufacture need a choice of antifoam chemistries; a silicone and silicone-free range lets them test both.
opening_questions: Do you make enzymes in-house or through contract fermentation partners?
Which antifoam chemistries are in your process development toolbox?
Are you scaling any new fermentation products in 2027?

top.what_they_make: Family-owned German producer (since 1900) of organic and conventional wheat starch, cold-swelling starches and flours, and proteins.
top.why_silitex: Wheat starch and gluten separation foams; the organic lines may need an organic-compatible antifoam (BIOTECH: FDA, BIO).
opening_questions: How do you control foam in wheat starch and gluten separation?
Do your organic lines need organic-compatible processing aids?
Is purchasing handled by the plant?
top.avoid: Mid-size family company: a good fit for a direct European supplier.

top.what_they_make: Italian producer of gelatine and collagen peptides from bovine hides, fish skin and pig skin, exported to 52 countries for pharmaceutical, food, cosmetic and nutraceutical uses.
top.why_silitex: Gelatine extraction, filtration and evaporation foam heavily; food and pharma grades need food-contact antifoams.
opening_questions: Where do you need foam control: extraction, evaporation or the hydrolysis of peptides?
Do pharma grades limit antifoam chemistry?
Is a local Italian supplier an advantage for you?

top.what_they_make: Develops and produces yeast-based flavours, yeast protein, food enzymes and fermentation-derived flavours.
top.why_silitex: Yeast, yeast protein and enzyme fermentations all need antifoam dosed into the broth. CPL 350 ET and SILIFOOD 30 carry kosher certificates on silitex.it.
opening_questions: Which of your plants make yeast protein, and how is foam controlled there?
Do your enzyme lines have restrictions on silicone carry-over?
Do you need kosher-certified processing aids?
top.avoid: Large private group with global procurement.

top.what_they_make: Supplies whey protein concentrate and other whey derivatives from selected fresh-cheese whey to sports nutrition, dairy and food customers.
top.why_silitex: An Italian whey processor is a natural short-supply-chain customer for food-grade simethicone antifoams.
opening_questions: What antifoam do you use in whey concentration and drying?
Do your customers require kosher-certified processing aids?
Would a local Italian supplier simplify logistics for you?

top.what_they_make: Whey-based ingredients for functional, health and performance nutrition (high-protein foods, clear protein beverages, whey permeate).
top.why_silitex: Whey processing (ultrafiltration, evaporation, spray drying) foams heavily; simethicone emulsions suit dairy. CPL 350 ET and SILIFOOD 30 carry kosher certificates on silitex.it.
opening_questions: Where in whey fractionation do you need foam control?
Are kosher and halal mandatory on processing aids?
Which site evaluates new antifoams?
top.avoid: Large cooperative group; stringent qualification.

top.what_they_make: Italian company with over 50 years in eggs and egg products, running a fully integrated, traceable production chain.
top.why_silitex: Egg breaking, pasteurisation and egg-powder drying generate foam.
opening_questions: Where does foam affect your egg-product lines?
Do you need kosher-certified processing aids?
Who handles processing aids at your plants?

top.what_they_make: Austrian producer of dairy ingredients from organic cow and goat milk and whey for advanced nutrition.
top.why_silitex: Organic dairy and whey processing still needs approved antifoams in evaporation and drying.
opening_questions: Do organic rules restrict which antifoams you can use?
Where does foam limit throughput in your plant?
Who approves processing aids?
top.avoid: Organic certification may limit silicone use; check first.

top.what_they_make: Specialty fats for food: plant-based oils and fats, chocolate fillings and coatings (filling fats, CBEs, coating fats, milk-fat replacers) and soluble fibre.
top.why_silitex: Fat processing and soluble-fibre (soy) extraction lines may need antifoams for oily or aqueous media.
opening_questions: Is there foam in your soluble-fibre or fat-processing lines?
Do your confectionery customers ask you about release or anti-stick solutions?
Is purchasing handled in Belgium or by the Japanese parent?
top.avoid: No food-grade release agent in the catalogue; lead with antifoams.

top.what_they_make: Refines brewers' yeast into products for human and animal nutrition, with in-house research laboratories.
top.why_silitex: Debittering, autolysis and drying of brewers' yeast foam; a kosher, FDA vegetal compound fits the food and feed lines.
opening_questions: Which processing steps foam most on brewers' yeast?
Do the feed and food lines use the same antifoam?
Is purchasing local or through the Asahi group?
top.avoid: Shares stand 31A38 with Asahi Group Foods (same group); purchasing may be at group level.

top.what_they_make: Enzyme producer with over 120 years in enzyme science; says it is the world's number one non-GM enzyme producer, serving dairy, dairy alternatives and other food uses.
top.why_silitex: Non-GM enzyme fermentation needs antifoams with clean food-contact status. CPL 350 ET and SILIFOOD 30 carry kosher certificates on silitex.it.
opening_questions: Do your European operations ferment locally or import enzymes from Japan?
What antifoam constraints apply to your non-GM and kosher claims?
Would you evaluate a vegetal antifoam in a pilot fermenter?
top.avoid: Production may be outside Europe; check the decision point first.

top.what_they_make: French producer of freeze-dried lactic cultures for dairy and plant-based applications, with over 50 years of experience.
top.why_silitex: Producing lactic cultures means fermenting biomass before concentration and freeze-drying, and foam control with food-safe antifoam is needed. CPL 350 ET and SILIFOOD 30 carry kosher certificates on silitex.it.
opening_questions: Which antifoam do you use in culture propagation today?
Do your plant-based cultures need vegetal, non-silicone processing aids?
Who decides on processing aids at your plant?

top.what_they_make: Italian maker of vegetable fats and oils, margarines, UHT plant-based toppings, ice-cream bases, pastes and chocolate/compounds; five plants (three in Italy).
top.why_silitex: Anhydrous E900 silicones (SILIFOOD 100/1000) are designed for oily media; check PDMS fluids for release and processing in their bakery and confectionery lines.
opening_questions: Do you use antifoam in oil processing or the topping and whipping lines?
Do you supply release oils to bakery customers, and what is in them?
Who in R&D evaluates additive suppliers?
top.avoid: The catalogue has no food-certified bakery release agent; FLUIDO DI SILICONE is food-contact only on selected viscosities, so confirm the grade before offering it.

top.what_they_make: Supplies multifunctional yeast derivatives and culinary powders based on natural baker's and torula yeast to food, biotech, human-health and animal-health markets.
top.why_silitex: Torula and baker's yeast fermentation, autolysis and spray-drying of yeast extracts all foam. CPL 350 ET (kosher, FDA) targets yeast manufacturing.
opening_questions: Where is foam control hardest: fermentation, autolysis or evaporation?
Are you open to qualifying a European second-source antifoam?
Which certifications must a processing aid have (kosher, halal, FDA, organic)?
top.avoid: Part of ABF Ingredients, which may run group supply contracts.

top.what_they_make: Enzyme solutions for baking, protein modification, fruit processing and pulp & paper, among other industries.
top.why_silitex: Enzymes are made by submerged microbial fermentation, where antifoam dosage and how it affects downstream filtration both matter.
opening_questions: Which antifoam types are validated in your fermentation and recovery steps?
Does silicone affect your ultrafiltration membranes?
Who owns processing-aid qualification: R&D or production?
top.avoid: ABF Ingredients group; confirm site-level purchasing.

top.what_they_make: Dutch farmer cooperative (more than 2,000 members) making potato starch and a range of other potato-derived products.
top.why_silitex: Potato starch and potato protein isolation runs on large foaming process-water streams.
opening_questions: Which antifoam types are used in starch and protein recovery today?
Is there a sustainability push toward vegetal antifoams?
When is your next processing-aid review?
top.avoid: Cooperative with long-standing supplier relationships.

top.what_they_make: Sugar beet processor (formerly Suiker Unie) making sugar and sugar specialities and turning all parts of the beet into natural ingredients.
top.why_silitex: Sugar factories use antifoams in beet washing and diffusion during every campaign.
opening_questions: Which antifoam types do you use in beet washing and diffusion?
Is the antifoam tender annual, before each campaign?
Do you need a silicone-free option for any side streams?
top.avoid: Supply probably contracted per campaign; timing matters.

top.what_they_make: Austrian group turning agricultural raw materials into industrial products; segments include sugar, starch and fruit.
top.why_silitex: Sugar campaigns, potato and maize starch processing, and fruit preparations all need antifoam.
opening_questions: Which division has the biggest foam problem: sugar, starch or fruit?
Is antifoam bought centrally or per site?
Is there interest in silicone-free options for bioethanol or starch side streams?
top.avoid: Shares stand 31D80 with Austria Juice; one visit covers both.

top.what_they_make: AGRANA subsidiary; a leading maker of fruit-juice concentrates, beverages and flavour concepts.
top.why_silitex: Fruit washing, pressing and juice concentration foam; SILIFOOD 1600 and RIMAX S are positioned for fruit washing.
opening_questions: Where do you dose antifoam: washing, pressing or evaporation?
Do you need kosher-certified processing aids for juice exports?
Is supply set by AGRANA group or locally?
top.avoid: AGRANA group purchasing may apply.

top.what_they_make: Yeast extracts and other natural-fermentation solutions for food manufacturers; part of Lesaffre, which has worked in fermentation since 1853.
top.why_silitex: Yeast-extract production (fermentation, autolysis, evaporation) needs constant foam control; offer a kosher, FDA vegetable compound or a silicone-free route. CPL 350 ET and SILIFOOD 30 carry kosher certificates on silitex.it.
opening_questions: Which steps foam most for you: propagation, autolysis or concentration?
Would a silicone-free, 100% vegetal antifoam help your clean-label positioning?
Is antifoam bought per plant or through Lesaffre group purchasing?
top.avoid: Global group with an established antifoam supply base: position as a second source for a single site.

top.what_they_make: Founded in 1928, makes plant-based products for food, animal-nutrition and technical uses (potato and pea starches, proteins and fibres).
top.why_silitex: Potato starch and protein recovery from potato fruit juice is one of the foamiest food processes.
opening_questions: How do you control foam in potato fruit-juice and protein recovery?
Do you need a non-silicone option for the protein streams?
Who qualifies new processing aids?

top.what_they_make: Cooperative processing beet, sugarcane, cereals and alfalfa through 41 industrial sites in 15 countries.
top.why_silitex: Beet washing, diffusion and juice purification, and starch wet-milling, are classic foam points; RIMAX S/1000 S are positioned for sugar manufacturing and beet washing.
opening_questions: Which steps foam most in your beet campaign: washing, diffusion or carbonatation?
Do you split antifoam tenders by sugar and starch sites?
When does your next processing-aid tender open?
top.avoid: Big group with tender-based supply; aim for a site trial or second-source slot.

top.what_they_make: Listed Chinese yeast company (founded 1986) mass-producing yeast and yeast derivatives, with twelve factories and a major yeast-extract business.
top.why_silitex: Yeast propagation and yeast-extract fermentation is foam-heavy; CPL 350 ET is positioned by Silitex specifically for yeast manufacturing. CPL 350 ET and SILIFOOD 30 carry kosher certificates on silitex.it.
opening_questions: Which antifoam chemistry do you run in propagation today: vegetable, polyglycol or silicone?
Do your European or export plants require kosher or halal antifoams?
Who qualifies processing aids: plant QA or central procurement?
top.avoid: Large group, likely with locked central supply and domestic sourcing; aim at a specific plant or export line, not the whole group.

top.what_they_make: One of Europe's leading sugar producers (since 1870; Diamant and Kölner Zucker brands), turning sugar beet into sugar products at sites across Europe.
top.why_silitex: Beet sugar processing is a core antifoam application named in the RIMAX product pages.
opening_questions: Where do you see the most foam: washing, diffusion or evaporation?
Do you want polymer-based or silicone antifoams in sugar processing?
Who manages processing-aid tenders across your plants?

top.what_they_make: Family fruit-processing business (since 1923) making juices, purées, concentrates and custom blends for the food and beverage industry.
top.why_silitex: Fruit washing, pressing and concentration foam, and an Italian food-grade antifoam maker is a natural local partner.
opening_questions: Where is foam a problem: washing, pressing or concentration?
Do you need kosher processing aids for exports?
Who handles purchasing for your Italian and foreign sites?

top.what_they_make: Plant-based ingredient group with over 90 years in food (starches, polyols, plant proteins).
top.why_silitex: Wet milling, plant-protein extraction and polyol fermentation all need antifoam.
opening_questions: Which plants or processes would consider a second-source antifoam?
Is there a European plant-protein line with foam issues?
Who in central procurement handles processing aids?
top.avoid: Very large group with global supply agreements; aim for a niche or second-source position.

top.what_they_make: Produces Solein, a protein made from a natural, non-modified single-cell organism, for the food industry.
top.why_silitex: Continuous gas fermentation of single-cell protein needs dependable foam control as the factory scales.
opening_questions: How is foam managed in your gas-fermentation reactors?
Which antifoam chemistries are acceptable in Solein's regulatory dossiers?
Are you qualifying suppliers for scale-up?
top.avoid: Novel-food dossier may lock in specific processing aids; ask before pitching a switch.

top.what_they_make: Belgian family business, one of the largest producers of frozen potato products for private labels.
top.why_silitex: Potato washing, cutting-water and blanching foam, and frying oil foams too; anhydrous E900 silicone is used in oily media.
opening_questions: Do you dose antifoam into frying oil or the potato process water?
Which antifoam do you use today, and who supplies it?
Is purchasing centralised across your plants?
top.avoid: Check EU additive rules for E900 in frying oils for their product category before quoting.

top.what_they_make: Italian industrial group doing primary processing of agricultural raw materials, making ingredients from soybean, sunflower, rapeseed, cereals and pulses.
top.why_silitex: Oilseed crushing, degumming and lecithin or protein lines involve foaming oil and water phases; anhydrous E900 silicones suit oily media.
opening_questions: Do you have foam problems in oil refining, lecithin or protein lines?
Do your organic lines need organic-compatible antifoams?
Who buys processing aids for your plants?

top.company: NIZO Food Research (incl. Biotechnology Fermentation Factory Ede)
top.what_they_make: Independent contract research and manufacturing organisation for food and health; runs what it calls Europe's largest open-access, food-grade pilot and scale-up plant.
top.why_silitex: A contract fermentation and scale-up plant runs many client processes and needs a range of food-grade antifoams in stock.
opening_questions: Which antifoams do you keep on hand for client fermentations?
Do clients specify antifoam, or do you choose?
Would a sample kit (silicone, vegetal, alcohol-based) help your pilot team?

top.what_they_make: Indian producer of enzymatic solutions for food, nutrition and other industries.
top.why_silitex: An enzyme maker with its own fermentation is a direct antifoam consumer; kosher and FDA status can help export-oriented plants.
opening_questions: Which fermentation scale do you run (solid-state or submerged)?
What antifoam do you use now, and is local supply a pain point?
Do your customers ask for kosher or halal on the processing aids?
top.avoid: Indian plants may favour local suppliers on cost; qualify volume and logistics first.

top.what_they_make: Multi-Latin company founded in 1956 producing yeast, yeast extracts and flavour enhancers, plus raw materials for bakery and food.
top.why_silitex: A yeast and yeast-extract producer is the textbook user for CPL 350 ET (kosher, FDA, positioned for yeast manufacturing).
opening_questions: Which antifoam do you run in yeast propagation now?
Do you import processing aids from Europe?
Would kosher certification help your export customers?
top.avoid: Plants are in Latin America; confirm whether a European supplier can serve them.

top.what_they_make: US producer of non-GMO pea proteins and other pulse ingredients, built over nearly 40 years.
top.why_silitex: Pea protein wet extraction and isoelectric precipitation foam; BIOTECH and CPL 350 target vegetable extracts.
opening_questions: How do you control foam in pea protein extraction?
Do you require non-silicone or organic-compatible antifoams?
Do you have European production or partners?
top.avoid: Production is in the US; a European supplier needs a logistics case.

top.what_they_make: World's leading producer of Balsamic Vinegar of Modena PGI, also serving private label, industrial and food-ingredient customers from Modena.
top.why_silitex: Acetification and concentration of grape must can foam; an Italian food-grade antifoam supplier is a natural fit.
opening_questions: Do you have foam issues in acetification or must concentration?
Do PGI or organic rules limit which processing aids you can use?
Who buys processing aids: plant or group?
top.avoid: PGI or organic rules may restrict processing aids; check before proposing silicone.

top.what_they_make: Life-science company making biologically valuable molecules for pharma, nutraceutical and food; a leader in the API heparin.
top.why_silitex: Extraction and purification of biological molecules (heparin, chondroitin, collagen) foam; ANTISCHIUMA 3 and SILIFOOD 3000 are described for pharma use.
opening_questions: Where does foam affect your extraction and purification?
What regulatory documents do you need from an antifoam supplier for API processes?
Who approves processing aids at your plants?
top.avoid: API (pharma) processes need GMP documentation; confirm what Silitex can provide.

top.what_they_make: Producer of ingredients from natural sources (texturants, acidulants, minerals) for food, nutrition, health, home and personal care; headquartered in Basel.
top.why_silitex: Citric acid, xanthan and other fermentation products are high-volume, foam-intensive processes.
opening_questions: Which of your fermentations (citric, xanthan, gluconates) is most foam-critical?
Is antifoam contracted centrally or per plant (Austria, France, Canada)?
Would a kosher-certified vegetal antifoam fit your label commitments?
top.avoid: Large, mature fermenter: expect strict qualification and established suppliers.

top.what_they_make: HKEx-listed bio-fermentation manufacturer of amino acids (L-valine, L-leucine, L-glutamine, L-arginine, L-tryptophan), MSG, xanthan gum and gellan gum, hyaluronic acid and other products.
top.why_silitex: Very large amino-acid, MSG and xanthan fermentation volumes make heavy antifoam use.
opening_questions: Do you buy antifoams for any non-Chinese production sites?
Which antifoam types do you use in amino-acid fermentation?
Are kosher or halal processing aids required for your exports?
top.avoid: Huge Chinese producer that probably sources antifoam domestically on price; a lead for a niche or certified grade at most.

top.what_they_make: Global provider of amino-acid nutrition and health solutions, supplying clients in over 100 countries; founded in 2002.
top.why_silitex: Amino-acid fermentation is an antifoam-intensive process.
opening_questions: Do any of your plants buy imported antifoams?
Are certified (kosher, halal) processing aids required?
Who evaluates new processing aids?
top.avoid: Same caution as Fufeng: domestic supply and price-driven.

top.what_they_make: Makes casein and other enhanced proteins by precision fermentation for food and nutrition.
top.why_silitex: Precision-fermentation scale-up runs into foam early, and antifoam must not interfere with protein recovery. CPL 350 ET and SILIFOOD 30 carry kosher certificates on silitex.it.
opening_questions: Are you fermenting in-house or with a CMO, and at what scale?
Does antifoam carry-over affect your casein purification?
Are you still choosing processing aids for commercial scale?
top.avoid: Start-up volumes; long-term upside rather than immediate tonnage.
